overall: Washington DC is off to a hot start on July 2, with the current temperature at 84.2°F as of 07:45 ET and still climbing at +1.8°F/hr. forecast_obs_notes: NWP model agreement is exceptionally tight: GFS (104.0°F), ECMWF (103.9°F), and HRRR (103.7°F) are virtually identical, with NBM somewhat lower at 100.9°F. max_temp_prediction: Despite the META model's conservatism favoring a 90-93°F range, the atmospheric setup — clear skies, near-calm winds, anomalously high dewpoints, and unanimous NWP model consensus at 100-104°F — strongly supports a TMAX above 100°F. With temps already at 84.2°F at 07:45 ET and peak heating still 7+ hours away, there is ample time for the additional 15-20°F rise the models expect. For the active even-bucket market, the 94-95°F top bucket understates the likely outcome; I expect TMAX to land in the low-to-mid 100s, with confidence tilted toward the NWP consensus over the META model given the extraordinary model agreement and observational trajectory.
